title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 234
paragraphs: So the Greeks at Thermopylae fought. Xerxes then summoned Demaratos and questioned him, first saying this: “Demaratos, you are a good man — I infer it from the truth of your words, for everything you said turned out just as you said. Now, however, tell me: how many Lacedaemonians remain, and how many of them are like these in matters of war? Or are they all of them such?” Demaratos said: “O king, the total number of Lacedaemonians is great and their cities are many; but what you wish to know, you shall learn. In Lacedaemon there is the city of Sparta, with about eight thousand men; these are all equal to those who fought here. The other Lacedaemonians are not equal to these, but they are good men too.” Xerxes then said, “Demaratos, by what means can we get the better of these men with the least trouble? Come, explain this to us — you know the course of their counsels, since you were once their king.”
